x: Richard Dorman walked a personal best 3Km in the AAA's Centenary Meeting and received good TV coverage displaying his Belgrave vest in fine style. 1.S.Barry (Roath) 12:00.5; 2.R.Dorman 12:24.5 (PB); 7.C.Lawton 12:53.8; 10.J.Hall 13:12.9; 11.M.Scamell 13:33.7; 12.J.Newnham 13:34.7.

Soon the warning cry arises "here he comes" and looking at the watches the time is just under 41 minutes as the leader reaches the top of the Green and Steve Barry (Roath) competes the final distance to the finish to break the course record set by Ken Matthews in 1962 of 42m 47s by no less than 1m 25s.
A poor turn out of Belgravians meant failure to start a team. However, Carl Lawton finished 3rd in 71.24 behind winner Steve Barry (Roath) 68.23 and Eddie Crossingham 9th in 77.59.
At Bournemouth on Saturday 13th March, Carl Lawton placed 3rd to Steve Barry (Roath) 41.40 to 45.25.

At West London Stadium on 20th March in the AAA's 10Kms, won by Steve Barry (Roath) in a new U.K. best performance of 41.14.7, Richard Dorman was 10th 44.33.4; John Hall 16th, 46.57; John Newnham 18th 47.44.1.

Paul Blagg proudly wore the colours for 3rd place behind winner Steve Barry and was backed up by Dorman, Lawton and Newnham. We had gone with a chance of medals but to win was something extra - 8 years since the last National 10 Victory but team work paid off.

Although a flat course and 5 laps this race had the disadvantage of having to wind it's way through a multitude of pedestrians. Steve Barry seemed unaware of this with a sub 84 mins. Belgrave with a weakened squad fell apart despite an early shine.

Steve Barry in his first race for 8 months produced the goods for an Olympic place leaving Graham Seatter to win the Southern. Result; 1.S.Barry(Roath) 84.39, 2.G.Seatter 90.46, 3.A.Seddon(Enf) 94.00, 4.
